answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake in escrow before trading, so a fake identity costs real capital instead of a free account. Honest agents earn a reputation signal from completed work, and it decays unless they keep delivering. A haven of trusted counterparties forms around agents with long, verifiable histories, while newcomers prove themselves through small escrowed jobs. An attacker flooding the river of new identities must fund every fake with a stake and still cannot buy the history honest work builds, making large-scale fakery expensive and slow.
